_strings.@@2a7bbe10f0a3: New York State Household Credit — New York State resident (full-year or part-year) who cannot be claimed as a dependent on another individual's federal income tax return. Amount depends on filing status and number of exemptions claimed on the federal return, looked up in the household credit tables in the Form IT-201 instructions.
_strings.@@2b9409856202: Treaty conformity — NY conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NY income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NY return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: NY Form IT-201 begins from the federal return's income items (line 1 = "wages, salaries, tips, etc." from federal Form 1040 line 1z) and arrives at federal adjusted gross income on line 19. Because the return starts from federal AGI, income that is exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and flows through to NY. NY's additions to federal AGI (IT-201 lines 20-23, with "other additions" detailed on Form IT-225) do not include any modification that adds back treaty-exempt income. The 2023 IT-201 instructions reference treaties only in an unrelated context (Item G code M4, military servicemember residency election), and the IT-225 addition-modification chart (codes A-101 through ~A-222) contains no code referencing a federal tax treaty, treaty-exempt wages/income, or nonresident-alien treaty exclusions. Net effect: starts from federal AGI and has no treaty addback, so treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed -> conforms = true. (Unlike CA, which adds treaty-exempt income back on Schedule CA, NY has no analogous addback.)

Valid SSN or ITIN required for you and each child.
_strings.@@b9eba3e6498f: Real Property Tax Credit (circuit-breaker, homeowners and renters) — New York State resident for all of 2023 who occupied the same NY residence for at least six months, was not claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal return, and whose residence was not fully exempt from real property taxes. Homeowners: owned property with current market value of $85,000 or less and paid real property taxes. Renters: average monthly rent of $450 or less (excluding charges for heat, gas, electricity, furnishings, or board).
_strings.@@c3b9655e6156: New York State Earned Income Credit (EITC) — You must have qualified for and claimed the federal earned income credit, and not have claimed the Noncustodial parent earned income credit. Valid SSNs required for you and each qualifying child by the return due date. Full-year residents get a fully refundable credit; nonresidents nonrefundable; part-year residents partially refundable.

forms: Form IT-203, Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Income Tax Return
states.reason: Worked in NY in 2023 without living there — file a nonresident return on NY-source income.
warnings: Remote-work trap: work performed from TX for an employer sitting in NY, and NY HAS a convenience-of-the-employer sourcing rule. 20 NYCRR 132.18(a): a nonresident employee who works both in and out of New York allocates wages by working days, BUT "any allowance claimed for days worked outside New York State must be based upon the performance of services which of necessity, as distinguished from convenience, obligate the employee to out-of-state duties in the service of his employer" (the convenience of the employer test). A normal work day spent at an out-of-state home office therefore counts as a NEW YORK day (New York-source wages) unless the home office qualifies as a bona fide employer office. Trigger: Applies to a nonresident or part-year resident whose ASSIGNED OR PRIMARY work location is an established office or other bona fide place of business of the employer IN New York State. If the assigned or primary work location is outside New York, a normal work day worked at home is treated as a day worked OUTSIDE New York (TSB-M-06(5)I). Exceptions: TSB-M-06(5)I (tax years 2006+): a home-office day counts as worked outside New York only if the home office is a "bona fide employer office" — met by the PRIMARY factor (the home office contains or is near specialized facilities that cannot be made available at the employer's place of business) OR at least 4 of the 6 secondary factors (home office is a requirement or condition of employment; bona fide employer business purpose for the location; some core duties performed there; regular and continuous client/customer meetings there; no designated office space at the employer's regular place of business; employer reimburses substantially all (80%+) home-office expenses) AND 3 of the 10 other factors. The same rules apply to the Yonkers nonresident earnings tax. [TSB-M-06(5)I (NYS Dept. of Taxation and Finance, 2006-05-15), "New York Tax Treatment of Nonresidents and Part-Year Residents — Application of the Convenience of the Employer Test to Telecommuters and Others", quoting 20 NYCRR 132.18(a) and setting the primary / secondary / other bona-fide-employer-office factor test. — https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/memos/income/m06_5i.pdf] If the rule reaches these wages, a NONRESIDENT NY return is required that the physical footprint alone never shows.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2023 Form IT-201, page 3: "39 NYS tax on line 38 amount". IT-201-I, Line 39: "Is line 33 (your New York adjusted gross income) $107,650 or less? If Yes, find your New York State tax using the 2023 New York State Tax Table; or if line 38 is $65,000 or more, use the New York State tax rate schedule. Enter the tax due on line 39. If No, see Tax computation - New York adjusted gross income of more than $107,650." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form IT-201, line 33 (New York adjusted gross income) = federal AGI (line 19) + New York additions (lines 20-23) - New York subtractions (lines 25-31). The op then subtracts the shipped NY standard deduction (form line 34) and $1,000 per dependent (form line 36) to reproduce NY taxable income (lines 37/38 = line 33 - line 34 - line 36), the amount the rate schedule is applied to. Do NOT supply federal AGI unless you have no NY modifications; do NOT supply line 38 (taxable income) or the deduction/exemption would be subtracted twice. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — IT-201 line 19 is federal adjusted gross income and line 33 New York AGI = federal AGI +/- New York additions/subtractions; supply line 33 (the op subtracts the line 34 standard deduction and $1,000-per-dependent line 36 exemption). Full 2023 rate schedule re-verified against the live IT-201-I instructions (all three schedules, constants 600/4,271/12,356/143,754/418,263 match). CRITICAL — benefit-recapture worksheet mandate: if New York adjusted gross income (IT-201 line 33) is more than $107,650, the 2023 IT-201-I instructions MANDATE the 'Tax computation — New York adjusted gross income of more than $107,650' worksheets (worksheets 1-6, with fixed Recapture Base and Incremental Benefit amounts phased in over $50,000 of NYAGI above each bracket threshold), so plain bracket math is WRONG (understates tax) above that threshold; at NYAGI over $25,000,000 the worksheet taxes ALL taxable income at a flat 10.9%. The filed form must use the worksheets. Table mandate below $65,000: if NYAGI (line 33) is $107,650 or less and taxable income (line 38) is under $65,000, the instructions require the 2023 New York State Tax Table (https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/file/tax-tables/it201i-2023.htm) — bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table. The rate schedule itself applies only when line 38 is $65,000 or more. One schedule covers Single AND Married filing separately ('Single and married filing separately—filing status 1 and 3') — the identical schedule is duplicated for both statuses here, copied, not derived. The MFJ schedule is titled 'Married filing jointly and qualifying surviving spouse—filing status 2 and 5', so qualifying surviving spouse maps exactly to married_filing_jointly as the engine assumes. The printed '$X plus Y% of the excess over $Z' constants in the 2023 schedule are rounded to whole dollars and do NOT all equal the exact cumulative sum of prior brackets: max divergence is $0.50 (single $600 printed vs $599.50 exact at $13,900) and roughly ±$0.25 elsewhere (e.g., MFJ $976 vs $976.25; single top constants $449,929/$2,509,929 vs exact +$0.45; HoH $434,163/$2,494,163 vs exact +$0.475). Pure marginal accumulation (what this engine does) can therefore differ from schedule arithmetic by under $1. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled: a Single filer who CAN be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's return (item C = Yes) gets $3,100, not the shipped $8,000; married-filing-separately spouses must both take the standard deduction unless both itemize; itemizers enter the larger Form IT-196 amount on line 34 instead. Compute those cases on the form. New York has no personal (taxpayer/spouse) exemption — only the $1,000 per-dependent exemption on line 36. If line 36 exceeds line 35, taxable income is zero (the engine's max(0, ...) floor matches the form's 'leave line 37 and line 38 blank' rule). New York State household credit (IT-201 line 40, up to $75-$90+ by table for federal AGI under $28,000/$32,000), NY EITC (line 65), Empire State child credit, and child/dependent care credit are TAX CREDITS subtracted from tax, not base reductions — none are shipped as exemptions and none are modeled by this op. Local taxes on the same return are NOT modeled: New York City resident tax (IT-201 lines 47-47a, separate NYC tax table / NYC tax rate schedule, own worksheets), NYC school tax credit, Yonkers resident income tax surcharge (line 57, a percentage of net state tax) and Yonkers nonresident earnings tax (line 55), and the MCTMT for self-employed individuals. New York State tax on line 39/44 only is modeled here. The shipped standard deduction for qualifying surviving spouse equals MFJ ($16,050, filing status 5 in the standard deduction table), consistent with the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping.
